Indikator 12 evaluates critical clinical outcomes for patients, encompassing both the risk of severe bleeding and mortality rates. According to the 2023 data, the indicator tracks the proportion of newly diagnosed atrial fibrillation patients who develop severe bleeding within one year across regions and hospitals [^src1]. The 2024 data shifts the focus to 1-year mortality proportions across various geographic health clusters [^src2]. The broader methodological framework, data collection procedures, and additional clinical indicators for the Danish Atrial Fibrillation registry are extensively documented across the 2023 and 2024 annual reports [^src3] [^src4] [^src5] [^src6] [^src7] [^src8] [^src9] [^src10] [^src11] [^src12] [^src13] [^src14] [^src15] [^src16] [^src17] [^src18] [^src19] [^src20].

In the 2023 assessment of severe bleeding, no hospital or region successfully met the clinical standard, with the "Standard opfyldt" (Standard met) column uniformly showing 0% compliance across all entities [^src1]. [[kolding-sygehus|Kolding Sygehus]] recorded the highest proportion of severe bleeding at 6.0%, while [[steno-diabetes-center|Steno Diabetes Center]] reported the lowest at 0.0% [^src1]. Nationally, [[danmark|Danmark]] experienced a slight improvement, with the severe bleeding rate decreasing from 3.3% in 2020/21 to 3.1% in the current reporting period [^src1]. Some outliers exist in the 2023 data, such as Næstved, which reported a 5.0% bleeding rate but with a very low patient count and a wide confidence interval (0.1-24.9%), and Samsø Sundheds og Akuthus, which reported 0.0% in the current period but had a 50.0% rate in 2020/21 [^src1].

The 2024 mortality data reveals significant geographic disparities in 1-year survival outcomes [^src2]. [[sundhedsklyngen-nykoebing-f|Sundhedsklyngen Nykøbing F]] recorded the highest 1-year mortality rate at 16.6%, followed closely by [[sundhedsklynge-soenderjylland|Sundhedsklynge Sønderjylland]] at 15.2% [^src2]. In contrast, [[sundhedsklyngen-suh|Sundhedsklyngen SUH]] achieved the lowest mortality rate at 9.2%, with [[sundhedsklynge-byen|Sundhedsklynge Byen]] performing well at 9.9% [^src2]. At the national level, Danmark demonstrated a positive trend, with 1-year mortality dropping from 13.1% in both 2020/21 and 2021/22 to 12.5% in the current year [^src2]. [[region-hovedstaden|Region Hovedstaden]] also showed consistent improvement, decreasing from 13.3% in 2020/21 to 11.9% currently [^src2]. However, this downward trend was not universal; [[region-sjaelland|Region Sjælland]] saw its mortality rate rise to 13.0% in the current year from 12.8% in 2020/21, despite a peak of 14.1% in 2021/22 [^src2].
